scope: Published as a GitHub release asset and pinned by digest; the release URL is durable but not immutable, so the pinned sha256 is what makes the download trustworthy rather than the address it came from.

components.name: pali-canon-dense-vectors
components.basis: 4802 indexed HTML entries, 4795 rendered texts plus 7 collection indexes from this manifest's own build receipt, the redirections excluded because the ingest skips them, one vector each at the encoder's 384 dimensions and the profile schema's default float32 vector datatype. Rights exclusions and a non-canonical selection policy can only lower the count, and a float16 profile halves the width

components.name: pali-canon-dense-graph
components.basis: Qdrant's published capacity formula hnsw_size = points x m x 2 x 4 bytes x 1.2 at its default m of 16 (https://qdrant.tech/documentation/capacity-planning/); the collection adapters.Qdrant.create builds keeps the graph on disk and overrides no HNSW parameter

components.name: pali-canon-dense-payload
components.basis: Qdrant's published disk_size = points x avg_payload_size x 1.5, whose 1.5 covers backend storage overhead. Every point carries the same four-field record adapters.Qdrant.put builds, 393 bytes compactly encoded at this archive's widest entry index of 9492

components.name: pali-canon-passage-spans
components.basis: the article-spans artifact stores each article's extracted blocks, spans and representative compressed at zlib level 6. The only measured constant, 3190 bytes per article in oracle_content.precompute, was sampled from English Wikipedia and does not transfer to this archive's entries; sampling this archive is what would quantify it. The builder publishes whatever it reaches and stops at its own --min-free-bytes floor, so an unreserved shortfall costs coverage rather than the install

components.name: dense-index-headroom
components.basis: the ~20% disk headroom the same Qdrant capacity page recommends, taken over the vector, graph and payload components it covers: the write-ahead log, snapshots and the optimizer's temporary segments. The article-spans artifact is a SQLite file outside the vector store and is deliberately not in this sum

components.name: shared-service-runtime
components.basis: indexing writes into the shared content state and the shared Qdrant store, and adds no per-pack runtime working set; the service's own bounded stores (CONTENT_SNAPSHOT_MAX_BYTES, CONTENT_FAILURE_LOG_MAX_BYTES) belong to the installation rather than to any one pack and are not multiplied by it

components.name: archive-second-copy
components.basis: prepare_native hardlinks the verified archive into the content state, so the original occupies its pinned artifact bytes once; a content state on another filesystem cannot hardlink and needs that many bytes again, which is a layout choice this manifest cannot see

Original library: https://suttacentral.net/

SuttaCentral dedicates the translations in this archive to the public domain under
Creative Commons Zero 1.0. CC0 asks for nothing in return, so the attribution below is
given rather than owed: a dedication of this size is a gift, and its authorship should
stay legible to anyone who reads from it.

  Bhikkhu Sujato    the four nikayas and much of the Khuddaka collection
  Bhikkhu Brahmali  the Vinaya Pitaka
  John Kelly, Ayya Soma, Bhante Suddhaso, Kovilo Bhikkhu
                    further texts of the Khuddaka collection
  Jessica Walton    co-translator of the Theragatha

This archive carries the English translations only. Their segmentation and markup are
keyed to the Mahasangiti edition of the Pali, which the translators worked from; that
Pali text is not included here. Each article names its translator and links to the
passage it was rendered from, and every article carries this same dedication in its
own footer.

One English translation in the source data, the Patna Dharmapada, is published under
CC BY-SA 3.0 rather than CC0 and is excluded from this archive; so are translations
whose root text is not Pali. The build receipt records both exclusions by count.
